dedupe_keys.name: dataset of toward a scec broadband platform with 3d low frequency synthetics bbp 3d

description: Ke Xu and Kim Olsen at San Diego State University publish synthetic ground motions and analysis scripts for validating three-dimensional low-frequency additions to the SCEC Broadband Platform. The Zenodo collection is free under CC BY 4.0. It contains ten-source ensembles for the 1989 Loma Prieta, 1994 Northridge and 2019 Ridgecrest earthquakes, comparing one- and three-dimensional results, plus individual sensitivity runs. Outputs include acceleration and velocity histories, station lists, source parameters and Python goodness-of-fit scripts. These benchmarks can test seismic loading assumptions in infrastructure fragility simulations. The related model-scec-broadband-platform record covers the earlier platform, but does not explicitly include this separate BBP 3D dataset. The documented low-frequency comparisons extend to one or two hertz and should not be mistaken for the full broadband range. One description labels velocity units as metres, not metres per second, so units require confirmation. Archives were not opened and simulated histories were not compared against observations.
